summary: Add monotonic constraints to improve calibration for Top 25% predictions
rationale:
The model shows severe overfitting (8% train-validation gap: 70.77% vs 62.90%) and Top 25% accuracy needs improvement. Adding monotonic constraints constrains the model to respect logical relationships between features and win probability, improving calibration without removing features (learned from iteration 1 failure that removing features harms underdog performance). Three key features with clear directional relationships were constrained:

1. striking_differential (+1): Landing more strikes than you absorb should monotonically increase win probability
2. recent_improvement_score_diff (+1): If fighter A is improving more than fighter B, A should have higher win probability
3. prospect_momentum_score_diff (+1): Higher momentum should monotonically increase win probability

This regularization through monotonic constraints should reduce overfitting and improve Top 25% accuracy while maintaining all features that underdogs depend on.
expected_effect: Expected to improve Top 25% accuracy through better calibration. Monotonic constraints reduce model flexibility, which should help close the train-validation gap (currently 8%) and improve generalization. By constraining these features to have positive relationships with win probability, the model will make more logically consistent predictions, particularly in high-confidence buckets. Underdog performance should be maintained since all features are preserved.
